_meta.collected: 2026-08-30 through 2026-08-31, two rounds (an initial 16-book list, then a 20-item numbered list plus resolved series/aggregate statements)
_meta.notes: The only rater used for every scoring test in docs/scoring-test-protocol.md so far. See that doc's opening section on why conclusions from a single rater are provisional. 5 ratings added 2026-09-02 once catalog growth filled gaps that blocked them at collection time: Lord of Chaos (WoT book 6, previously untagged, now fills the 'up to A Crown of Swords' range) and A Little Hatred/Best Served Cold (First Law World extras, previously untagged, now cover 'all of First Law world, loved'). Fool Moon and Grave Peril (Dresden Files books 2-3, previously untagged) resolve the earlier 'at least 3, liked all' ambiguity -- combined with Storm Front (book 1, already rated), these are almost certainly the 3 he meant. 24 more ratings added 2026-09-02 (later same day) from a third round covering the now-larger catalog. Two required judgment calls, both flagged to the repo owner rather than silently resolved: (1) Sword of Destiny included as 'liked' under 'the witcher books... up to Lady of the Lake, liked all but the last' -- reasonable given reading order, but not explicitly named; (2) The Golden Compass and The Amber Spyglass both set to 'loved' by analogy with The Subtle Knife (already 'loved' on file) -- no prior 'Golden Compass' rating was ever actually found on file or in the session transcript despite the repo owner believing he'd given one, so this is an assumption, not a recovered fact. Several titles mentioned this round are NOT in the catalog yet and were NOT added (nothing to guess from): The Lady of the Lake (Witcher 5, would be it_was_okay), Calamity (Reckoners 3, loved), King of Thorns/Emperor of Thorns (Broken Empire 2-3, loved), Grey Sister/Holy Sister (Book of the Ancestor 2-3, loved), Valor (Malice's actual sequel, loved), The Desert Spear/The Daylight War/The Skull Throne/The Core (Demon Cycle 2-5 -- notably the last-book 'hated' rating has nowhere to attach yet), Rise of Empire (Theft of Swords' sequel, disliked). Also NOT added: Saga, Vol. 1 (graphic novel, loved) -- genuinely in-catalog and tagged, but whether comics are in v1 scope at all is an open product question raised by the repo owner, not a rating decision. 'The Devils' (Joe Abercrombie) is its own standalone series, not First Law world, so 'any First Law I hadn't rated' added nothing new -- all catalog First Law titles were already rated. UPDATE (2026-09-02): repo owner raised a real methodological point while reviewing a qualitative recommend() test -- this project's rating scale measures ENJOYMENT, not perceived literary quality, and his own instinct sometimes conflates the two (rating a well-written book he didn't especially enjoy higher than his actual enjoyment, out of respect for its craft). Concretely: The Poppy War was originally it_was_okay, but on enjoyment alone (plus a retrospective souring after DNFing its sequel) he judged it a genuine dislike -- changed to disliked. The Dragon Republic (Poppy War's sequel, DNF'd about a quarter in for the same reason -- a heavy-handed anti-violence message, independently corroborated by a friend who read Babel, same author, and noticed the same pattern) added as disliked, its first real rating. Promise of Blood (Powder Mage #1) added as loved -- read and loved the whole original trilogy plus a novella, but this specific title had never been rated before (missed when reviewing the catalog earlier). The rest of Powder Mage (The Crimson Campaign, The Autumn Republic, and the unspecified novella -- repo owner didn't name which one) are NOT added: confirmed not yet in the catalog at all, not just untagged (see docs/project-log.md for whether/how they get ingested). UPDATE (2026-09-02, later): confirmed the Powder Mage novella he read is Forsworn (Powder Mage #0.1), rated liked -- added to the catalog as bibliographic data only (`20260902070000_targeted_ingestion_forsworn_novella.sql`), but not yet tagged, so this rating can't be added to `ratings` until it is (same as The Crimson Campaign/The Autumn Republic above). UPDATE (2026-09-03): Dawnshard (Stormlight Archive novella) added as liked -- read it, missed rating it earlier; surfaced when it appeared in a qualitative recommend() review round 2. Kings of Paradise added as loved -- also surfaced by that same review round; repo owner confirmed loved (his 'wasn't it logged already' turned out to be a false memory, it genuinely wasn't on file until now). UPDATE (2026-09-03, later): repo owner listed ~19 more remembered books, all bibliographically ingested this round (`20260903170000_targeted_ingestion_mathias_priority_list.sql`) and 22 ratings added here. Valor confirmed already in the catalog (John Gwynne's, not Brian McClellan's, per his own correction) -- just needed the rating, added as loved. Licanius trilogy: The Shadow of What Was Lost was already in the catalog and already rated liked (untouched); The Light of All That Falls was already in the catalog but unrated, rating added (liked); An Echo of Things to Come was missing entirely, ingested and rated liked. Ender's Shadow was already in the catalog and already rated loved -- confirmed correct, not touched, nothing new added for it. Kings of Paradise's two sequels (Kings of Ash, Kings of Heaven) ingested and rated loved, matching his already-on-file 'loved the whole trilogy' rating for book 1 (which was NOT touched). The Grey Bastards (loved) and its confirmed sequel The True Bastards (hated, confirmed via search -- not 'The Barrow Bastards' or similar guess) both ingested. Covenant of Steel trilogy (The Pariah=liked, The Martyr=loved, The Traitor=loved), Aching God (liked, sequels deliberately not added), The Vagrant (liked) and The Malice (liked) both by Peter Newman -- disambiguated from John Gwynne's unrelated 'Malice' (different hardcover_id/series, already on file as loved, untouched) -- The Justice of Kings (liked), Prince of Fools/The Liar's Key/The Wheel of Osheim (Red Queen's War trilogy, all loved), Blackwing (liked, sequels not added), Firestarter (loved), and the Time Master trilogy (The Initiate/The Outcast/The Master, all liked -- repo owner flagged this as a softer memory ('I remember reading... and liking it'), used liked as instructed but confidence is lower than usual here) were all ingested and rated. Two real judgment calls: 'I'm Afraid You've Got Dragons' was named as Peter McLean's but Hardcover has no such title under that author -- the actual book by that exact title is Peter S. Beagle's (2024); ingested under Beagle and rated hated per instruction, flagged in case this isn't the book he actually meant. The Wandering Inn (pirateaba) was ingested as a single representative entry (Hardcover's highest-popularity, series-position-1 listing) rather than picking among its many individual volume entries, rated hated. NOT rated despite being ingested: One Word Kill (Mark Lawrence) -- he said only 'didn't resonate well with me', which is genuinely ambiguous between disliked and it_was_okay; book added to the catalog but no rating recorded, needs the repo owner to pick a label directly. UPDATE (2026-09-03, later): repo owner resolved all three open items from this batch. Confirmed 'I'm Afraid You've Got Dragons' is indeed Peter S. Beagle's, not a misattribution to fix. One Word Kill: he DNF'd it, rated disliked (added above -- DNF counts as a real dislike signal, not left unrated). The Wandering Inn: confirmed hated is correct and strongly so -- he listened to ~5 hours of the audiobook before stopping. Kings of Paradise's orphaned series_id was fixed separately (see 20260903180000_link_kings_of_paradise_to_series.sql) -- now correctly linked to Ash and Sand as book 1, matching its two sequels. UPDATE (2026-09-03, later): Ninth House (Leigh Bardugo) added as disliked -- read it, no strong feelings either way but found it boring and DNF'd, surfaced when it appeared in a qualitative recommend() review round 3. Hard-Boiled Wonderland and the End of the World (Haruki Murakami) added as loved -- already in the catalog and already tagged (genre: sci_fi + fantasy) from an earlier session, just never rated; surfaced by the repo owner himself after 1Q84 (a different Murakami book) appeared in that same review round. UPDATE (2026-09-03, later still): City (Clifford D. Simak) added as liked -- another remembered book, surfaced after reviewing the fantasy/sci-fi split lists. Newly ingested (`20260903230000_targeted_ingestion_city_simak.sql`), bibliographic only, not yet tagged -- rating recorded now so it activates automatically once tagged, same pattern as the earlier remembered-books batch.
